evidence.excerpt: A 400 V / 48 V, 500 W DC–DC converter using 650 V GaN HEMTs and switching at 1 MHz is characterised for conducted and radiated electromagnetic emissions per CISPR 32 Class B limits. Conducted emissions were measured using a line-impedance stabilisation network in the 150 kHz–30 MHz band. Differential-mode and common-mode noise contributions were separated using a current probe and a 180° hybrid coupler. Radiated emissions were measured in a semi-anechoic chamber in the 30 MHz–1 GHz band. Without input filtering, differential-mode conducted noise at 1 MHz exceeded the Class B quasi-peak limit by 18 dBµV. A two-stage LC input filter reduced differential-mode noise by 24 dB and common-mode noise by 19 dB, achieving compliance with 4 dB margin. Parasitic capacitance of the heat-sink was identified as the dominant common-mode noise path and a Y-capacitor between heat-sink and DC bus reduced common-mode noise by a further 7 dB. Correlation between near-field scan results and far-field measurements is discussed.
